subject: Math
prompt: The triangle inequality theorem states that the sum of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the length of the third side. If a triangle has side lengths of $7$ and $15$, which inequality represents the possible lengths, $x$, of the third side of the triangle?
explanation: Choice A is correct. According to the triangle inequality theorem, the sum of any two sides of a triangle must be greater than the third side. Let the side lengths be $7$, $15$, and $x$. We must satisfy three conditions: (1) $7 + 15 > x \implies 22 > x$ (or $x < 22$), (2) $7 + x > 15 \implies x > 15 - 7 \implies x > 8$, and (3) $15 + x > 7 \implies x > 7 - 15 \implies x > -8$. The third condition is always true for any positive length $x$, and the condition $x > 8$ is stronger. Combining $x < 22$ and $x > 8$, we get the compound inequality $8 < x < 22$.
